scientific_assessment.reason: Aggregate-only calibration lets the once-elicited Qwen prior drive behavior. Calibrated to a 0.30 base rate, it admits about a third of agents and picks entrants who are productive 46 to 48 percent of the time, against 33 percent under the hand rule, in every replicate of every world. As a probability forecast it is no better than the hand rule, and its selectivity leaves pooled learners about 30 percent less evidence, so they end up worse in the interaction worlds. The verbalized prior admits everyone. It produces the most evidence and the best pooled nonlinear learning, and it is the only LLM variant that improves neighbor-scale learning beyond a no-knowledge prior.
